source_text: Ut et de locis secundum propositum exequar, circus Soli principaliter consecratur. cuius aedes in medio spatio et effigies de fastigio aedis emicat, quod non putauerunt sub tecto consecrandum quem in aperto habent. qui spectaculum primum a Circa [habent] Soli patri suo, ut uolunt, editum affirmant, ab ea et circi appellationem argumentantur. plane uenefica eis utique negotium gessit hoc nomine, quorum sacerdos erat, daemoniis et angelis scilicet. quot igitur in habitu loci illius idololattias recognoscis ? singula ornamenta circi singula templa sunt. oua honori Castorum adscribunt qui illos otio editos credendo de cygno Ioue non erubescunt. delphines Neptuno uomunt, columnae Sessias a sementationibus, Messias a messibus, Tutulinas a tutela fructuum sustinent; ante eas [tres arae, trinis deis parent, Magnis Potentibus Valentibus. eosdem Samothracas existimant. obelisci enormitas, ut Hermateles affirmat,, Soli prostituta. scriptura eius unde eius et census: de Aegypto superstitio est. frigebat daemonum concilium sine sua Matre Magna; ea itaque illic praesidet euripo. Consus, ut diximus apud metas, sub terra delitescit Murcias. eas quoque idolum fecit: Murciam enim deam amoris uolunt, cui in illa parte aedem uouerunt. animaduerte, Christiane, quot nomina inmunda possederint circum. aliena est tibi religio, quam tot diaboli spiritus occupauerunt. de locis quidem locus est retractandi ad praeueniendam quorundam interrogationem. quid enim, inquis, si alio in tempore circum adiero, periclitabor de inquinamento ? nulla est praescriptio de locis. nam non sola ista conciliabula spectaculorum, sed etiam templa ipsa sine periculo disciplinae adire seruus dei potest urguente causa simpli ci dumtaxat, quae non pertineat ad proprium eius loci negotium uel officium. ceterum et plateae et forum et balneae et stabula et ipsae domus nostrae sine idolis omnino non sunt: -totum saeculum satanas et angeli eius repleuerunt. non tamen quod in saeculo sumus, a deo excidimus, sed si quid de saeculi criminibus attigerimus. proinde si Capitolium, si Serapeum sacrificator uel adorator intrauero, a deo excidam, quemadmodummodum circum uel theatrum spectator. loca nos non contaminant per se, sed quae in locis fiunt, a quibus et ipsa loca contaminari altercati sumus: de contaminatis contaminamur.
thought_title: The circus as a place full of idols
orientation: Tertullian is now examining the places where the shows are held, arguing that the circus itself is consecrated to the Sun and filled with idols.
pass_a_gloss: So that I may also go through the places according to my plan, the circus is principally consecrated to the Sun. Its temple is in the middle of the space, and its image shines from the top of the temple, because they did not think that what they have in the open should be consecrated under a roof. They affirm that the first show was put on by Circe for the Sun her father, as they want it, and from her they argue the name of the circus. Clearly a sorceress certainly did business for them under this name, whose priest she was, for demons and angels of course. How many idolatries therefore do you recognize in the appearance of that place? The individual ornaments of the circus are individual temples. They ascribe the eggs to the honor of the Castors, who do not blush to believe that they were born from leisure from Jupiter the swan. The dolphins vomit for Neptune; the columns support Sessias from the sowings, Messias from the harvests, Tutulinas from the protection of fruits; before them three altars serve three gods, the Great, the Powerful, the Strong. They consider these the Samothraces. The hugeness of the obelisk, as Hermateles affirms, is prostituted to the Sun. Its writing is from where its origin is: it is a superstition from Egypt. The assembly of demons was cold without its own Great Mother; she therefore presides there over the canal. Consus, as we said, hides under the ground at the turning posts, Murcia. It made these too an idol: for they want Murcia to be a goddess of love, to whom they vowed a temple in that part. Notice, Christian, how many unclean names have possessed the circus. Foreign to you is the religion which so many spirits of the devil have occupied. About the places indeed there is a place for treating beforehand to prevent the question of certain people. For what, you say, if I go to the circus at another time, will I be endangered by defilement? There is no prescription about places. For not only those meeting-places of shows, but also the temples themselves can be entered without danger to discipline by a servant of God when a simple cause urges, provided that it does not pertain to the proper business or office of that place. But the streets and the forum and the baths and the inns and our own houses are not entirely without idols: Satan and his angels have filled the whole world. Yet not because we are in the world do we fall away from God, but if we touch any of the crimes of the world. Therefore if I enter the Capitol, if the Serapeum, as a sacrificer or worshipper, I shall fall away from God, just as if I enter the circus or theater as a spectator. Places do not defile us by themselves, but the things that happen in places, by which we have argued that the places themselves are also defiled: by defiled things we are defiled.

choices.why: Keeps the passive force and the adverb 'principaliter' as 'principally' to show the Sun's primary claim on the place.

choices.term: uenefica eis utique negotium gessit hoc nomine
choices.english: a sorceress certainly did business for them under this name
choices.why: Preserves the sarcastic tone of 'utique' and the commercial metaphor of 'negotium gessit'.
rejected: a witch certainly managed this business for them

choices.why: Keeps the vivid, crude verb 'vomit' to match Tertullian's contempt for the idolatrous decoration.

choices.english: the hugeness of the obelisk ... is prostituted to the Sun
choices.why: Retains the shocking metaphor of prostitution to convey Tertullian's polemic against pagan consecration.
rejected: the great obelisk ... is dedicated to the Sun

choices.term: frigebat daemonum concilium sine sua Matre Magna
choices.english: the assembly of demons was cold without its own Great Mother
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of coldness for lack of worship and the possessive 'sua' to mock the demons' attachment to Cybele.
rejected: the council of demons was inactive without its Great Mother

choices.english: foreign to you is the religion
choices.why: Preserves the emphatic fronting of 'aliena' and the dative of reference 'tibi' to address the Christian directly.
rejected: the religion is foreign to you

pass_b_english: Now let me continue with the places, as I proposed. The circus is chiefly consecrated to the Sun. Its temple stands in the middle of the space, and the Sun's image shines out from the temple's pediment, because they did not think that one whom they keep in the open should be consecrated under a roof. They claim that the first show was put on by Circe for the Sun, her father, as they would have it, and from her they derive the name of the circus. Clearly a sorceress certainly did business for them under this name, for the demons and angels whose priestess she was. How many idolatries, then, do you recognize in the appearance of that place? Each ornament of the circus is a separate temple. The eggs they assign to the honor of Castor and Pollux, those who are not ashamed to believe they were born from a swan, from Jupiter. They cast forth dolphins to Neptune. The columns bear images of Sessia from the sowings, Messia from the harvests, Tutulina from the protection of fruits. Before them three altars serve three gods: the Great, the Powerful, the Strong. They consider these to be the Samothraces. The hugeness of the obelisk, as Hermateles affirms, is debased to the Sun. Its inscription, and from it its tribute, is superstition from Egypt. The assembly of demons was incomplete without its own Great Mother; so she presides there over the canal. Consus, as we said, is hidden underground at the turning posts; Murcia is there too. He made even them into an idol: they claim Murcia is a goddess of love, to whom they dedicated a temple in that part. Take note, Christian, how many unclean names have taken possession of the circus. Foreign to you is the religion that so many spirits of the devil have occupied.

Now is the place to discuss the places themselves, to forestall some people's question. "What then," you say, "if I go to the circus at some other time, will I be endangered by its defilement?" There is no prescription about places. For not only these meeting-places of the shows, but even the temples themselves, a servant of God can enter without danger to his discipline when a simple cause compels him, provided only that it does not pertain to the business or function proper to that place. Besides, the streets and the forum and the baths and the inns and our very houses are not entirely without idols: Satan and his angels have filled the whole world. Yet it is not because we are in the world that we fall away from God, but if we touch any of the world's crimes. Therefore if I enter the Capitol or the Serapeum as a sacrificer or worshiper, I shall fall away from God, just as I would as a spectator at the circus or theater. Places do not defile us by themselves, but the things done in them, by which we have argued the places themselves are defiled. From the defiled we are defiled.

problems.fix: Consus, as we said, hides Murcias underground at the turning posts.

problems.quote: The turning posts too have become an idol: they claim Murcia is a goddess of love
problems.source_quote: eas quoque idolum fecit: Murciam enim deam amoris uolunt
problems.why: Subject is Consus, not the turning posts; 'eas' (the posts) he made into an idol by dedicating a temple to Murcia there.
problems.fix: He made even them into an idol: they claim Murcia is a goddess of love
problems.ruling: Latin 'eas quoque idolum fecit' shows Consus made the posts idols; English shifts agency to the posts and omits Consus.

problems.why: Latin says "to the Sun, his father" (or the Sun's father), not "her father"; gender and relationship are altered.
Latin means "they vomit dolphins to Neptune" (people offering dolphins), not dolphins vomiting.
problems.ruling: Latin 'delphines Neptuno uomunt' means 'they vomit dolphins to Neptune'; English reverses agency, making dolphins the subject.

fixed: Changed 'her father' to 'his father' because the source 'Soli patri suo' refers to the Sun as father of Circe, not her father.
Changed 'The dolphins vomit for Neptune' to 'They vomit dolphins to Neptune' because the source 'delphines Neptuno uomunt' means people vomit dolphins as an offering to Neptune.

problems.fix: They claim the first show was presented by Circe to the Sun, her father, as they would have it, and from her they derive the name of the circus.
problems.ruling: Latin 'Soli patri suo' links 'suus' to Circe, meaning 'her father', not 'his father'.

problems.quote: The columns support Sessia from the sowings, Messia from the harvests, Tutulina from the protection of fruits
problems.why: Three goddesses (Sessia, Messia, Tutulina) abruptly introduced with columns 'supporting' them; syntax compressed.

problems.why: 'Prostituted' is strong but odd for an obelisk; likely means 'dedicated in a degraded way' or 'misapplied'.

fixed: Glossary: 'Murcias' is the oblique case of 'Murcia'; standardizing to 'Murcia' in the gloss avoids implying two figures.
Unreadable: 'They vomit dolphins to Neptune' misreads 'delphines Neptuno uomunt'; 'uomunt' here means 'cast forth' as offerings, so clarified.
Unreadable: 'The columns support Sessia...' compresses 'columnae Sessias... sustinent'; the columns bear images of the goddesses, so expanded.
Mistranslation: 'prostituted' for 'prostituta' is too strong; 'debased' better conveys the sense of misapplied dedication.
Unreadable: 'Consus, as we said, hides Murcias underground' misreads the source; Consus is hidden underground, and Murcia is a separate idol nearby.

problems.quote: The assembly of demons was cold without its own Great Mother
problems.why: 'Cold' here likely means 'incomplete' or 'lacking,' but modern reader reads temperature.
problems.fix: Use 'was incomplete' or 'lacked' instead of 'was cold.'

edits.old: The assembly of demons was cold without its own Great Mother
edits.new: The assembly of demons was incomplete without its own Great Mother

fixed: Changed 'was cold' to 'was incomplete' because the source 'frigebat' here means the assembly lacked or was deficient without the Great Mother, not that it had a low temperature.

dismissed.quote: They claim that the first show was put on by Circe for the Sun, her father, as they would have it, and from her they derive the name of the circus.
dismissed.why: Latin says the first spectacle was for the Sun, his father; English says it was for the Sun, *her* father, misassigning the father relation.
dismissed.note: Circe is the Sun's daughter, so 'her father' correctly renders 'patri suo'.
